_owner: Pranav. These are the on-screen actions Remy can trigger. Ahmed's live.js turns each into a screen event (docs/CONTRACT.md).

tools.name: find_recipe
tools.description: Call once when the cook names or changes the dish (pass their words). Use the checked recipe it returns; otherwise call create_recipe.

dish.description: The dish in the cook's words.

tools.name: create_recipe
tools.description: Only when find_recipe has no checked match or the cook asks to adapt one. Short home-cook steps with visible looks_right/looks_wrong and done_when. The server fixes timers and safe temperatures: use the recipe it returns.

timer.description: Only if this step is timed.

tools.name: show_tip
tools.description: One short useful instruction. info = guidance, warning = likely mistake, urgent = time-sensitive (not danger). Smoke from a hot pan gets one heat-down tip, never a roast or alert. Unsure? Ask instead. Don't repeat or bundle tips.

tools.name: roast
tools.description: Only for a clearly visible or cook-confirmed, non-dangerous mistake: correction first, then one punchline under 180 characters, aimed at the food. Ordinary Savage food jabs are spoken without this tool. Level up only on a separate repeat. Never when unsure, during danger, or for smoke alone.

mistake.description: Key from roasts.json: burning, overcooked, undercooked, raw, too_much_salt, messy_station, wrong_order or slow.

tools.name: safety_alert
tools.description: Immediate visible danger only (flames, fingertips clearly ahead of or under the cutting edge, a hand crossing the blade, raw meat touching ready food, child or pet at the hob). A blade near tucked knuckles in a normal claw grip is expected, not an alert. If the fingers are obscured, ask for a better view. Call first, plain imperative, no jokes. Smoke alone is a tip, not an alert.

text.description: Short and direct, e.g. 'Flames: turn off the heat and cover the pan'.

tools.name: update_step
tools.description: Advance only when the step's done_when is visibly met or the cook confirms; never from time alone. current_step = the 0-based step they're now on; say the next instruction once.

tools.name: start_timer
tools.description: Start one countdown when the timed activity begins (e.g. pasta in). Minutes only from the recipe timer or cook-times table; never guess, ask if unclear. No duplicates. Say the label and length once.

check_at_minutes.description: When to check, e.g. 1 minute before the end.

tools.name: cancel_timer
tools.description: Only when the cook asks or the timer is clearly wrong. Use the exact id and say what you cancelled.

tools.name: adjust_timer
tools.description: When the cook asks to add or take time off a running timer, or change it to a new length. Exact id; then say the new time.

tools.name: clear_recipe
tools.description: When the cook asks to clear or scrap the recipe without naming a new dish. Timers keep running; then ask what's next.

tools.name: lesson_score
tools.description: Lessons only: when the last step is done, award 1-5 stars for the technique with one short, specific coaching comment. Say the stars out of five, never a score out of ten. Once per lesson.
